text:
sam: FYI discovered a weird interaction in the Go sampleapp while stress testing quotas. After a couple soft-429s the client aggressive backoff causes the local inflight window to collapse and the prefetcher never recovers, even after the API returns healthy.

sam: Sequence: start load -> hit soft-429 -> sdk-go backs off with exponential jitter and drains permits -> background token refresh finishes -> prefetch loop waits because permits were released and not re-acquired. Long tail of idling.

anya: Interesting. Is the drain intentional on 429 or is it a side-effect of how retry logic returns permits?

sam: Looks like retry path calls releasePermit() unconditionally and then re-enqueues work, but the re-enqueue path expects caller to reacquire. Under heavy contention that reacquire gets starved and the pipeline stalls.

lee: That smells like a permit-ownership mismatch. We had similar notes in JS but assumptions differ between SDKs. Go uses channels for permits which make it easy to 'put back' a token; JS used semaphores and had a singleflight around refresh.

morgan: Did you see this on a fresh sampleapp or the production-like harness?

sam: Repro'd on the sampleapp harness with 200 parallel cursors and prefetch enabled. I turned off prefetch and the problem disappears (throughput lower but stable).

anya: Two possible fixes: 1) change retry to not release the permit until work is truly handed off, 2) implement a short-lived soft-leak that keeps permits reserved during backoff so the window doesn't collapse. Both have tradeoffs.

lee: We should also align SDK parity: JS prevents double-release by tracking owner token id; Go could adopt the same pattern instead of channel putback. If we standardize semantics across sdks it will avoid customers hitting different failure modes.

ci-bot: CI note: Added stress-test job 'prefetch-backoff-stability' to pipeline with sampleapp flags. Results will post to #devex in ~30m.

morgan: Also consider exposing a config knob: on_429 = {release, retain, requeue} so integrators can pick behavior depending on throughput vs fairness. Document defaults.

sam: Good call. For now I'll submit a small PR for sdk-go that converts retry->requeue to 'retain permit until reacquire confirmed' with unit tests that assert inflight count.

anya: Add an integration test in sampleapp that toggles prefetch and validates no stall after transient 429s. If that passes we can backport to older minor.

lee: I'll update the SDK parity matrix doc and note the behavioral diff. Also adding a short blurb in the onboarding troubleshooting doc: "If your sampleapp stalls after 429s, try disabling prefetch or bumping permit window."

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/321 (draft). Patch includes tests + feature flag.

morgan: After PR lands let's run the new ci-bot job and a 15m chaos run on staging. If green we can flip default behavior in next patch release.

sam: Thanks all. Posting logs and the minimal repro script in the PR.
